settings.scope: documented, safe, reusable mod and pack authoring surface, proved inside the gate
settings.whatThisMilestoneDidNotDo: No game process was launched for M4. evidence/m4/linux-process-matrix.json records that as gameLaunch.occurred false rather than as prose, and every consequence of it is a deviation or a risk below rather than a caveat inside a closed row.

M4-W1.evidence: ravel-sdk's mod-facing facade and the #[declare_mod] macro, with examples/minimal-mod as the crate an author copies and examples/minimal-mod/src/boundary.rs as the compile-pass/fail suite. tests/conformance/tests/sdk_boundary.rs derives the author boundary from the dependency closure Cargo.lock resolves for ravel-sdk rather than asserting it, so the gate recomputes what an author may reach instead of trusting a list. The row's own wording — that authors need no loader internals or Java — is what that suite checks. What it does not reach is publication: nothing is on a registry, so an author outside this checkout depends on the SDK by path, which docs/guide/limits.md states.

M4-W2.evidence: Public declaration APIs for registries, tags, resources and generated data, with examples/content-mod as the content example and a merged tag file built from every member's contributions. tests/conformance/tests/content_declarations.rs covers the row's three properties — declarations, conflicting claims, and generated output being the same bytes twice — against the loader's own pipeline. Nothing here reaches a game: no M4 process registered content in a running client or server.

M4-W3.evidence: Sides on the facade, the client-only side rule in ravel-core, packet contracts and their wire format in ravel-network, routing from a contract to the mod that owns it, and the client and server halves of test-mods/networking. tests/conformance/tests/sides_and_packets.rs checks both properties the row names. The row is closed on the abstractions it asks for and on nothing beyond them, and two limits are recorded as deviations rather than folded in here: a mod cannot send a packet, and the shipped host read no manifest, so no mod's declared sides were honoured by anything that runs. The second was repaired after the milestone closed and its deviation below names the repair; the row is left stating what it closed on.

M4-W4.evidence: Configuration, saved-data migration chains and inter-mod services on the facade; settings resolved and applied across a whole set; services opened in dependency order and closed on failure; a saved-data envelope built from an ordinary mod's declarations; examples/stateful-mod carrying all three. tests/conformance/tests/config_saves_and_services.rs covers the row's three properties — migration chains, service dependencies, and failure closure — and tests/conformance/tests/configuration.rs the settings half. What no gate reaches is composition from a package: the shipped host resolves a fixed set of mods against a constant configuration path.

M4-W5.evidence: ravel-pack declares a pack and checks its four closures, and tests/conformance/tests/pack_closure.rs drives every one of them through ravel_pack::validate, which is the only thing that produces a writable pack. ravel:verify-example-pack runs the pack example as its own process and compares the written tree both against a list the gate holds independently and against the example's own report. The write half is what is closed; nothing in this repository reads a written pack, which is recorded as an owed obligation below.

M4-W6.evidence: The one directory under tests/fixtures/public/versions/ holds a second version's data this repository invented for the purpose, and crates/ravel-minecraft-adapter/src/generate/mod.rs stages it through the same generator the pinned version goes through, asserting that what comes out names the second version and nothing of the first. verify_version_boundary in tools/ravel-xtask/src/lib.rs sweeps crates/ for either version's name and for every game class name either version's data supplies, with each permitted occurrence named and its excuse failing when it stops matching. Those two are what M4-W6 proves. The row's own wording — general crates compiling and testing without version-specific edits — is proved as those two properties and not as a general crate executing against the second version's table, which is recorded as a deviation below.

M4-W7.evidence: docs/guide/ is the public author's guide, tests/conformance/tests/guide_snippets.rs compiles every Rust block in it through examples/guide-snippets, cargo xtask package digests refreshes and checks a manifest's digests with ravel:verify-example-package running the check on the package an author copies, and test-mods/waystone-ledger is the original mod a fresh agent built from those documents with no internal access. The row assumed public author documentation existed and none did, so W7 wrote the guide before its own gate's premise could hold; the fresh-author run then found defects in the facade and in the guide, which are repaired in this tree. The limits that run surfaced are stated in docs/guide/limits.md and are deviations below rather than caveats inside this row.

M4-W8.evidence: The global Linux gate and the process matrix are recorded — evidence/m4/linux-process-matrix.json holds every gate process with its exit status, and commands and tests below hold the run itself. The independent review this row also requires has run and has closed: evidence/m4/review.md holds every recorded verdict verbatim, and the standing verdict is a pass returned on the tree the repairs answering the round before it left, with nothing repaired after it. That round's one new finding is non-blocking and is carried as a deviation below rather than fixed, deliberately, so that the pass certifies the tree its reviewer actually read; the deviation names the escape, names that the enumeration in the tree today is correct, and names who closes it. review.result below is pass and review.record binds the bytes that say so, which is what ravel:verify-milestone:m4 exits 0 on and is the whole of what closure asserts here.

deviations.summary: A mod cannot send a packet. M4-W3 shipped packet contracts, a wire format, encoding, decoding and routing from a contract to the mod that owns it, and every refusal in that surface is checked. What does not exist is the leg after encoding: no wire adapter is written, no launch path moves a byte between a client and a server on a mod's behalf, and Mod::receive_packet has no caller in a running game. So a declared packet is a specification of what a mod will send rather than something a mod sends. It is disclosed where an author meets it — crates/ravel-sdk/src/network.rs:132, docs/guide/README.md:12 and docs/guide/limits.md:19 all say so — and M4-W3's row is closed on the abstractions ROADMAP.md's Output column asks for and not on delivery. Owner: the wire adapters ROADMAP.md places after the abstractions; no M4 work package owns them and none claimed to.

The shipped host read no manifest, so M4 proved no mod's declared sides were honoured by anything that runs. At closure crates/ravel-composed-host/src/lib.rs wrote both lifecycle entries by hand and hardcoded a constant configuration path, under a section headed for exactly this. The mapping from a validated package set to lifecycle entries was production code and did read a manifest's sides — ravel_loader::admitted — and nothing in a launch path called it, because that host discovered no package and validated none. What M4-W3 proved was therefore the rule and the pipeline, checked in tests/conformance/tests/sides_and_packets.rs, and not the rule taking effect in a launch. The sides half was repaired after the milestone closed, which ROADMAP.md's M4-W3 row records in the same shape: every member now ships the package manifest it is packaged under, the composed host admits the whole set through ravel_loader::admitted rather than writing entries by hand, a server-only member proves the rule in the direction the client-only one cannot, and ravel_bootstrap_runtime::side asks the JVM which distribution it was started from instead of assuming a client. This entry stands rather than being deleted because it states what was true at closure, which is the tree the recorded review pass certifies. What the repair did not reach is discovery: the manifests are compiled in rather than found, so a package sitting in an instance directory is still read by nothing, and M4-W4's configuration composition stays fixed for the same reason — a settings document from a package the host does not know about is never read. docs/guide/limits.md states what is left to an author before they plan around it. Owner: package discovery in a launch path, which no M4 work package owned; M8's pack work is the first place it can honestly land.

The pack write-and-read-back round trip is unprovable by construction in this repository, so M4 claims the write half only. ravel_pack::validate is the only thing that produces a writable pack and tests/conformance/tests/pack_closure.rs drives every closure check through it; ravel:verify-example-pack then runs the example as its own process and compares the written tree against a file list the gate holds independently and against the example's own report. Nothing reads that pack back with Ravel. ravel_loader::open_configuration takes its documents from a caller-supplied map that no production caller fills, and M4 names no package for reading a pack at all. No claim is made here that a written pack holds correct bytes for a game to consume; what is checked is that the files the example says it wrote are the files on disk and that the manifest names a member. Owner: M8, which owns the complete Ravel pack and therefore the reading half.

No general crate is compiled or run against the second version's target table, and M4-W6's row must be read as the two narrower things it proves. The first is that the shared adapter's generator reads a second version's data through the same code path the pinned version goes through and emits that version's names and nothing of the pinned one, which crates/ravel-minecraft-adapter/src/generate/mod.rs asserts by staging the one directory under tests/fixtures/public/versions/ as if it were the pinned version. The second is that no file under crates/ spells either version's name or any game class name either version's data supplies, which verify_version_boundary sweeps for, with every permitted occurrence named and its excuse reported as stale when it stops matching. What neither shows is a general crate executing against the second version's table: one build compiles one table, and building the workspace against that second version would mean generating and pinning a second adapter output, which nothing in M4 did. M4's wording says the first two and does not imply the third. Owner: unowned; the first work package that needs two tables resident is where it becomes real, and none exists yet.

Only source.files and the provenance record are integrity-checked in a package, so anything declared elsewhere in a manifest and not also listed there ships unverified. Package verification hashes exactly those two sets. A configurationSchemas entry or a resources entry that is not also named under source.files is covered by no digest, and cargo xtask package digests --check will report a package with such an entry as current. This is the declared contract rather than a defect in the implementation of it — source.files is the declared set and the schema is explicit — but declared in the manifest and protected are different sets and an author will reasonably assume they are one, so docs/guide/limits.md tells them to list anything they want protected twice. Owner: unowned as a change to the contract; the disclosure is the whole of what M4 does about it.

The agent jar's persistence adapter reflective surface is still unpinned, and this manifest therefore claims no ADG-3 drift coverage for the agent jar. jvm/bootstrap/dev/ravel/jvm/Persistence.java resolves game classes and members by name through Class.forName, and what the pinned files cover is narrower than that surface rather than absent from it. Three of the class names it resolves — net.minecraft.client.Minecraft, net.minecraft.server.MinecraftServer and net.minecraft.world.level.storage.SavedDataStorage — are hook targets in minecraft/versions/26.1.2/hooks.toml and in mappings.lock, so a rename of one of those classes does land in a re-pin diff. What is in no pinned file is net.minecraft.world.level.storage.LevelResource, net.minecraft.util.datafix.DataFixers, every member name and arity the adapter resolves, the two LevelResource field constants, and the three-argument SavedDataStorage constructor. That is the gap, it is where Persistence.java's own comment at the lookup states it, and the drift gate reaches none of it. What does exist is verify_persistence_reflection in tools/ravel-xtask/src/lib.rs, which holds the jar's own sources to a declared set of class names and fails in both directions — but both sides of that comparison are Ravel's own, so it cannot see a game-side rename. Bringing the surface under stubs.toml and mappings.lock needs the stub-seed and lock re-pin ceremony against the pinned jar. ROADMAP.md's ADG-3 row records that no work package owns that ceremony, and because M4-W8 is where a drift claim over the agent jar would be made, this manifest states plainly that it makes none. Owner: unowned; ROADMAP.md's ADG-3 row is where that stays visible.

Every limit in docs/guide/limits.md is a gap M4 shipped with and disclosed rather than fixed, and the ones not already carried above are carried here so that no reader takes the guide as the softer statement. ravel-config resolves a configuration through an .ok() idiom, so a document that fails to parse is indistinguishable at that call site from one that is absent. Nothing checks that a package manifest's id and the id in a mod's #[declare_mod] agree, so a mod can be one identity to the loader and another to itself; docs/guide/conforming.md carries it as a pitfall. There is no command that validates a manifest — the schemas under schemas/ are the authority and are ordinary JSON Schema 2020-12, and Ravel ships no wrapper around a validator. Packaging tooling is one subcommand rather than a workflow: cargo xtask package digests and its --check mode, with no scaffold for a new mod crate and no publish step, against SPEC.md section 4.2's promise that an author publishes through supported tooling. PacketWriter::text and PacketWriter::bytes_field panic on a field of four gibibytes or more, which no decoded packet can reach and an author's own code can. Owner of each: the author-facing work M5 and later milestones schedule; none is owned by an M4 work package and none is claimed fixed.

M4's process matrix is not a launch and shares almost nothing with M3's record of the same name. Every row under processes in evidence/m4/linux-process-matrix.json is a gate process, and the row that is not sits under checksOutsideTheGate carrying a field named whyItIsNotAGateProcess that says so; verify_m4_process_matrix holds that separation in both directions. So the whole record is recomputable by a reader with the devenv shell and reaches nothing about Ravel inside a game. That is stated as gameLaunch.occurred false rather than as prose, because a record titled linux-process-matrix.json sitting beside M3's operator-run launch matrix is the most misreadable artifact in this milestone. Nothing in M4 needed a launch to be honest about what it built; what a launch would add is exactly the set of things the deviations above say M4 does not prove. Owner: no M4 work package; a campaign of M3-W7's shape is what would change it.

This manifest never spells the adjective M4-W6's fixture directory is named after, and the omission is deliberate rather than a style choice. verify_admitted_manifest in tools/ravel-xtask/src/lib.rs refuses a milestone manifest holding that word anywhere in any string, because a native milestone must not close on placeholder evidence. M4-W6's whole deliverable is a second version's data this repository invented, its directory under tests/fixtures/public/versions/ is named for exactly that, and naming the path here made the milestone gate refuse the manifest. The rule is left intact and this document works around it, which is stated here so the workaround is visible rather than silent: the fixture is real tracked data, evidence/m4/sdk-surface.json names its full path and is not subject to the rule, and a reader who wants the path should read it there. The rule is a false positive on this one milestone and narrowing it was refused, because a rule that refuses a word everywhere is checkable and a rule that tries to tell a placeholder from a fixture is a judgement no filter makes.

M4-W8 found one defect in the global Linux gate itself and it is fixed rather than only disclosed, but the gate is not what found it. flake.nix's scaffold check ran cargo run -p ravel-xtask -- verify scaffold with jq on its path and without check-jsonschema, which verify scaffold also shells out to, so in that check every milestone manifest reported that it could not validate the evidence schema and the schema rule the whole evidence set rests on ran nowhere outside the devenv shell. This deviation argued at first that the defect failed closed rather than falsely green because devenv tasks run ravel:verify-environment returned a nonzero status and named the reason. That reasoning requires the failing task to be inside the gate and it is not: ravel:verify does not run ravel:verify-environment, and nix/common.nix's after list is where that is decided. So the truth is narrower and worse. Throughout the whole period the flake's own check could not validate any evidence schema, devenv tasks run ravel:verify returned 0 and could not have returned anything else; the flake's check was red and the repository's gate never ran it; and the defect surfaced only because a person ran a task by hand. The defect predates M4 by every milestone manifest that existed before this one. flake.nix now supplies the validator, evidence/m4/linux-process-matrix.json records the task under checksOutsideTheGate rather than among the gate's processes, and verify_m4_process_matrix holds that separation in both directions so no later edit can move a non-gate row back among the gate's own.

The figures in this manifest and in evidence/m4/linux-process-matrix.json describe one gate run written down twice, which is the shape a figure goes stale in. verify_m4_gate_figures in tools/ravel-xtask/src/lib.rs reconciles the manifest's tests block against the record's gate block field by field on every ravel:verify, so an edit to one without the other fails the gate by name. The lists in evidence/m4/sdk-surface.json are held the same way by verify_m4_surface, which compares each one against the repository in both directions, and the record's own processes array by verify_m4_process_matrix, which compares it against ravel:verify's after list in nix/common.nix in both directions and refuses a nonzero exit status under a record that calls itself a pass. That last one was written because the first round of M4-W8's independent review showed the array was the one list in this evidence set no check reconciled: an invented process row and a flipped exit status both passed devenv tasks run ravel:verify-scaffold. What binds none of them is the run itself: the log is private, and revision.id is below the tip by construction because recording a result changes the tree that produced it. That ceiling is the one verify_recorded_run already records for every milestone and is not new here.

The guide's completeness claim is held to the first paragraph that carries it, and nothing requires there to be only one. enumerating_passage in tools/ravel-xtask/src/lib.rs finds the first paragraph of docs/guide/running.md containing the claim string and holds that paragraph's enumeration against the variants crates/ravel-network/src/lib.rs declares. So a verbatim duplicate of the claim placed anywhere earlier in the same file becomes the held passage, and the enumeration an author actually reads is held by nothing. The independent review measured that rather than arguing it: with a decoy paragraph naming all six WireError variants inserted near the top of the file and WireError::NotUtf8 deleted from the real enumeration, devenv tasks run ravel:verify-scaffold returned exit 0. What is true of the tree today is that the claim string occurs once, the enumeration under it names every declared variant, and the check fails by name when the claim is split from its list, when the claim is deleted with the list left intact, and when a variant is moved to another guide page — the review proved each of those three. So no author is misled and the escape needs a deliberate verbatim decoy to reach. This was left unrepaired on purpose. The repair is one line — require exactly one paragraph carrying the claim and treat a second as a violation, the same shape as the absent-claim branch already there — but landing it after the round that returned a pass would mean that pass certified a tree that no longer existed and a further round would be owed. Recording the hole is what lets the pass certify the tree its reviewer read. Owner: the next work package that touches verify_guide_enumerations, which closes it with that one line.

risks.summary: Withdrawn: this risk recorded that M4 was not closed, and it is discharged rather than reclassified. It stood on one condition — that the standing verdict in evidence/m4/review.md was a pass over a tree the repairs answering that round's own findings had since changed, so that a pass certifying the tree its reviewer read certified a tree that no longer existed. That condition is gone. The round recorded last read the tree those repairs left, reproduced its verdict verbatim in the record, walked every M4 row and every deviation against the tree, and returned a pass with an explicit statement that M4 is closeable on what it read. Nothing was repaired after it: its one new finding is carried as a deviation above rather than fixed, which is the choice that keeps the pass certifying the tree it read rather than owing a further round. review.result records pass, review.record binds the bytes that state it, and the verdict, review.result and this entry moved in one change. What closure asserts is ravel:verify and ravel:verify-milestone:m4 at exit 0 over this evidence and that standing verdict, and no more than that — the ceiling this manifest's last deviation states about attestation gates is unchanged by the milestone closing.

An author can build a conforming mod and cannot run it. That is the plain reading of the first three deviations taken together — no package discovery in a launch, no packet delivery, no pack read back — and it is stated as its own risk because each deviation on its own reads as a narrower gap than the three do together. What M4 delivers is an authoring surface that is documented, checked, and complete enough for a fresh author to build against it without internal access, which is what the milestone's purpose asks for. What it does not deliver is the moment an author sees their mod in a game, and no reader of this evidence should come away thinking otherwise.

Everything M4 proves, it proves in-process. There is no operator attestation to weigh here and no unrecomputable half, which makes this evidence set easier to check than M3's and narrower in what it reaches. The risk is that ease reads as strength: a green gate over in-process suites says the surface behaves as its own tests describe, and the tests were written by the same work that wrote the surface. The fresh-author run under M4-W7 is the one part of M4 that was not, and its findings are in the tree rather than in this sentence.

The JVM harness asserts Ravel's stubs against Ravel's reflection. ravel:verify-jvm runs the agent and its persistence adapter in a real JVM over stand-in classes under jvm/harness/persistence/, and those stand-ins declare the members Persistence.java resolves because Persistence.java needs them. So a game-side rename keeps the harness passing and lands at runtime as a refused world load or a skipped save rather than as a generation failure a diff would show. This is the runtime face of the unpinned reflective surface recorded as a deviation above, and it is recorded separately because a reader who trusts the JVM row of the process matrix is trusting exactly this.

review.reviewer: independent Claude reviewer (M4-W8, independent of the work under review; every round is reproduced verbatim in the record below, which is the one place that says how many have run)

attestations.statement: The gate run recorded under commands was made on this Linux machine, inside the devenv shell, on the tree revision.id pins. No game process was started for it and none is claimed: the Ravel code exercised is the workspace's own, including the agent and persistence adapter the JVM harness runs in a real JVM over stand-in classes.
